about: Narration for the video: python3 scripts/film-cut.py .stills-tmp/film --voice scripts/film-voice.json. Each line is spoken `at` seconds into its shot as cut. Numbers are CLAIMS rows 9 (12 collapses) and 11 (2,042 W > 1,500 W); the rest restates the caption panels and the game's own text. Synthetic voice (text-to-speech); the closing card says so.

lines.text: In twenty twenty-four, Nigeria's power grid collapsed twelve times.
When the lights die, someone has to decide what stays on.
Changeover puts that choice in your hands.
Night one. You're seated, hands only.
Pinch the fridge, carry it, and plug it into the inverter.
Then the fan.
The panel adds up every watt, and tells you how long the battery will last.
Every watt costs battery, and the inverter has a limit.
Add the clothes iron: two thousand and forty-two watts, on a fifteen-hundred-watt inverter.
Everything trips.
And you're back in the dark.
Some nights, there's a generator. It's tempting to just pull the cord.
But do it before isolating the mains, and the game refuses.
That generator would backfeed the street line, and could kill a line worker.
So here's the move built for eyes and hands.
Left hand out of tracking? Just look at the red isolator, and it lights up.
Your right hand throws the lever.
Now pull the cord,
and the generator runs.
Eyes choose. Hands act.
And it's a dead-man's switch.
The lever only holds while your eyes stay on the isolator.
Look away, and it springs back.
The safety rule becomes the game.
Keep the fridge cold through the night, till six in the morning,
and the flat opens into the room around you.
The fan turns over a sleeping child.
That's who you kept the power on for.
Every night is a new puzzle of watts, hours, and safety.
And every day, there's a new outage:
the same night for everyone, on the same date.
Win it to start a streak. Come back tomorrow to keep it alive.
Changeover. Keep the power on till dawn.
